listing.blurb: Crowd-controlled birds dodge neon high-rises over a sunset skyline, tapping upward to survive as columns scroll past.
listing.prompt: One-button flight: every person is a round little bird in their colour, and each press of 'flap' hops yours upward while gravity pulls it down; columns with gaps scroll past over a sunset city, birds that hit one tumble out, and the last bird flying wins. Make it a party game a whole room can follow from across the floor: bold shapes and bright colours on a dark ground, every player drawn in their own hue, big short labels (a score, GO!, the winner) in a heavy font, and a large, satisfying reaction on screen the instant anyone presses. It must work with one player or forty, scaling its lanes, seats or pieces to room.people and coping with people joining and leaving mid-round; play itself in a lively attract mode whenever nobody has pressed anything for a few seconds; and after a winner is shown, start the next round on its own. Keep it lean: game state in bounded arrays in room.state, nothing allocated inside hot loops, a steady 60fps at 1920x1080.
